metadata.title: [Perf][SM70] GLM-5.3: native mHC final stage for 2-8 tokens, cuBLAS KDA projection above one token
metadata.body:
## Purpose

GLM-5.3-Flash decode on 4x V100-SXM2 (TP4, MTP k=3, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs) spends its 38 ms step almost entirely in kernels (GPU 97% busy). A torch-profiler capture of 40 verify steps (4 tokens each) put two avoidable items on the list:

- the hyperconnection final stage (sigmoid/Sinkhorn mixes and RMSNorm) ran the Triton program for 2-8 tokens, one program per token: 35 us per call, 90 calls per step, 3.2 ms;
- the KDA input projection (6416 x 4096) took the exact native FP16 GEMV at every token count: 128 us per call at 4 tokens, 34 calls per step, 4.3 ms, where cuBLAS does the same GEMM in 74 us.

## Change

`vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/triton.py`: `sm70_mhc_pre_norm_from_staging` routes 2-8 tokens to `sm70_glm_mhc_pre_norm_out` by default (the op already handles any token count with one CTA per token) and asks for 1024 threads above one token. With the two policy fields unset (provenance `default`) the route takes the native op and 1024 threads; an explicit `mhc_native_verify` / `mhc_pre_threads` setting (environment or kernel config) still forces either choice. Nothing changes for one token or for more than eight. The two environment-variable descriptions are updated to say so.

`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/kda.py`: the exact native GEMV is taken for one token only; 2-8 tokens use the layer's standard projection (cuBLAS, FP32 accumulate).

No new environment variables, no new ops, no generic module touched.

## Not a duplicate

No open or closed PR changes the GLM-5.3 mHC final-stage dispatch above one token or the KDA projection's token-count gate (searched "mhc native", "pre_norm", "exact KDA", "glm53 decode").

## Test Plan

- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_sm70_fp16.py`: graph replay vs eager bitwise for 1/2/4/5/8 tokens (was 1/8); native vs Triton final stage for 2/3/4/6/8 tokens, FP32 mixes bitwise and normalized activations within FP16 rounding, with a perturbation guard; dispatch picks the native op for 1-8 tokens with the policy unset.
- `tests/models/glm5next/test_sm70_kda.py`: the exact-GEMV gate is single-token.
- Microbench of the native final stage in a CUDA graph at 4 tokens: 128/256/512/1024 threads.
- E2E A/B on 4x V100-SXM2-32GB, same build and checkpoint (GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 via #1102, TP4, MTP k=3, FP8 KV, 131K context): decode tok/s over 512-token greedy responses, and greedy output on a 7-prompt set incl. a 150-token prompt.
- ruff / pre-commit on the changed files.

## Test Result

- Native final stage in-graph, 4 tokens: 11.1 us (128 thr), 8.4 (256), 7.3 (512), 6.8 (1024); the Triton program averages 35 us in the same step.
- E2E decode (1 user): 82.4 tok/s with this PR vs 77.3 without, on the same tree (and 85.8 with #1102's updated expert kernel on top). Greedy output: 4 of 7 prompts identical, the rest diverge after 250+ characters, which is the pattern the previous build already shows against its predecessor (reordered FP32 accumulation under greedy decoding).
- Full-stack validation: `main` ec60883ad + #1125 (rebased) + this branch + #1161 + #1102, full CMake build: 147 tests pass across the five SM70 test files; E2E with the model card's serve command: 85.7 tok/s decode, 1 user.
- Unit tests: 66 passed, 1 skipped (`tests/kernels/test_mhc_sm70_fp16.py` + `tests/models/glm5next/test_sm70_kda.py`) on a full SM70 CMake build of `main` 4e5357b59 plus this commit, V100-SXM2-32GB.
- pre-commit: ruff 0.14.0 format and check clean on the changed files.

Gates before review:

- [x] Kernel tests against an independent oracle, failing under mutation (native vs Triton final stage with a perturbation guard; dispatch tests for default-on and explicit-off)
- [x] ruff on the changed files (no generic module touched, so the layering ratchet is unaffected)
- [x] Full wheel build (CMake path) and the test files above on it
- [x] E2E on 4x V100, CUDA graphs on: load, greedy comparison, decode speed (on the #1102 + #1125 integration tree, these two changes enabled through the policy fields, which is the same code path the unset default now takes)
